key_insight: An efficient SHAP-based explanation algorithm is introduced for Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) that produces covariate-informed, temporally-resolved attributions for load forecasting, enabling interpretable TSFM predictions without prohibitive compute cost.
problem_solved: Brings transparency to black-box TSFMs used in critical power-grid forecasting by providing reliable, computationally efficient feature attributions that account for temporal covariates and forecasting horizons—addressing trust, debugging, and regulatory needs in energy systems.
method: Design a SHAP computation strategy tailored to TSFMs that leverages model structure and temporal covariates to reduce sampling and evaluation overhead.
Use covariate-informed conditional sampling (or approximations) to compute temporally-resolved Shapley values for multi-horizon forecasts efficiently.
Validate the approach on load-forecasting tasks to demonstrate faithful attributions and substantial speedups over naive SHAP implementations.
impact: Makes large, general-purpose time-series models practical for use in critical infrastructure by providing interpretable, horizon-aware explanations—facilitating operator trust, model validation, and feature-level insights for ML practitioners in energy.
visual_elements: Schematic of a TSFM (encoder/decoder or transformer blocks) with overlaid SHAP attributions per time step and covariate icons.
Time-series plot: forecast vs. actual with stacked color bands showing per-feature SHAP contributions across the forecast horizon.
Bar/heatmap of feature importance over multiple horizons (feature × time) to highlight temporal shifts in drivers of load.
Performance chart comparing compute time and fidelity (explanation error) of the proposed SHAP method vs. standard SHAP baselines.
paper_title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
paper_authors: Matthias Hertel, Alexandra Nikoltchovska, Sebastian Pütz, Ralf Mikut, Benjamin Schäfer
